question: What happens if a caregiver mixes an ORS sachet in way too little water?

options.A: The child will refuse to drink because the solution is too cold
options.B: The extra salt crystals will kill all the bacteria in the stomach
options.C: The concentrated solution can worsen dehydration by drawing water into the gut
options.D: The medicine works twice as fast to stop the watery stool

explanation: Measurements matter! Too little water makes the drink too salty (hypertonic), which actually pulls body water out into the intestines and makes dehydration worse.

question: When cleaning a hospital room, what general direction should you follow?

options.A: From the cleanest areas to the dirtiest areas
options.B: From the floor upwards to the furniture tops
options.C: From the corners towards the middle of the ceiling
options.D: Randomly based on where the most visible dust is

explanation: Well done! Moving from clean to dirty ensures you don't drag heavy dirt and germs onto surfaces you just wiped clean.

question: Why is just handing out a new safety checklist usually not enough to change hospital practice?

options.A: Habits require ongoing reinforcement and audit to stick
options.B: Checklists are illegal in most healthcare settings
options.C: Doctors refuse to let nurses use checklists
options.D: Paper checklists take too much time to complete

explanation: Just giving out a new tool won't change daily habits unless there is proper follow-up, training, and regular performance checks.

question: What should the nurse do FIRST if a patient suddenly develops severe wheezing and increased breathing distress right after starting a nebulizer?

options.A: Wait ten minutes to see if the reaction goes away on its own
options.B: Stop the nebulizer treatment immediately and assess the patient
options.C: Ask the patient to lie flat and take deep, fast breaths
options.D: Turn up the air flow meter to make the mist spray faster

explanation: Worsening distress means a possible paradoxical bronchospasm, so stopping the drug is the immediate safety priority. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T7#GNS212_U2_T7_h7)

question: A community nurse is teaching rural farmers how to avoid hookworm. What is the best practical advice to share?

options.A: Wear protective footwear consistently when working outdoors
options.B: Avoid eating raw vegetables harvested from flooded river valleys
options.C: Take prophylactic antibiotics every morning before breakfast
options.D: Boil all drinking water for at least two hours before consumption

explanation: Since hookworm larvae wait in the soil to burrow through bare skin, putting on footwear is a simple, life-saving habit for farmers.

question: What is a direct benefit of proper funding at the primary health care level?

options.A: Consistent supply of essential drugs and vaccines
options.B: Construction of multi-story specialist surgical suites
options.C: Automatic promotion of all hospital administrators
options.D: Elimination of all diseases in the country

explanation: Adequate primary care funding directly ensures that basic medications and vaccine cold chains remain stocked and operational. [learn more](GST322_U5_T2#GST322_U5_T2_h3)

question: Where should a nurse look first to confirm which diluent is safe for a specific powdered medication?

options.A: The nursing station whiteboard schedule for the current shift
options.B: The patient's daily food and fluid intake preference chart
options.C: The general hospital cleaning and sanitation protocol manual
options.D: The official drug manufacturer package insert or pharmacy reference

explanation: The manufacturer package insert or hospital pharmacy guide provides precise instructions on approved diluents and safe mixing ratios. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T22#GNS122_U1_T22_h2)

question: What happens in the uterus right after a patient takes mifepristone?

options.A: Muscles relax completely to prevent any early spotting
options.B: The myometrium immediately begins violent cramping
options.C: The uterine lining breaks down and the cervix softens
options.D: Blood vessels expand to increase oxygen delivery to the fetus

explanation: Spot on! By blocking progesterone, mifepristone gets the uterus ready and softens the cervix before the second drug is even taken.

question: Why do many patients in Nigeria often report body tiredness rather than emotional feelings?

options.A: Local climate conditions cause chronic physical fatigue
options.B: Cultural tendencies often express emotional distress through physical symptoms
options.C: Physical illness is the only recognized health issue in the region
options.D: Psychiatric disorders are strictly forbidden from having emotional symptoms

explanation: Spot on! This is called somatization—it's very common for people to show emotional stress through bodily aches and tiredness. You are learning fast!

question: Why must a nurse repeat risk assessments throughout the entire pregnancy?

options.A: Pregnancy conditions and risks can change as the weeks progress
options.B: Mothers tend to forget their medical history if not asked often
options.C: Blood pressure and weight never stay stable for more than a month
options.D: Hospital guidelines require paperwork to be filled out weekly

explanation: A woman who starts her pregnancy healthy can develop complications like high blood pressure later on. [learn more](GNS225_U3_T8#GNS225_U3_T8_h1)

question: A patient with thick lung secretions refuses to drink water because of nausea. What is the best nursing action?

options.A: Force the patient to drink a full cup of water immediately
options.B: Report the fluid refusal and suggest IV hydration or anti-nausea medication
options.C: Document that the patient refuses care and leave the room
options.D: Stop all respiratory treatments until the nausea goes away on its own

explanation: Good hydration thins out thick mucus so it can be cleared easily. Addressing nausea and providing fluids through alternative routes helps maintain airway clearance. [learn more](GNS213_U2_T11#GNS213_U2_T11_h2)

question: Which of these food items must be strictly avoided on a low-fat diet?

options.A: Fresh apple slices
options.B: Butter and margarine
options.C: Plain boiled pasta
options.D: Steamed white rice

explanation: Correct! Butter and margarine are pure fats and need to be cut out to stay within a low-fat limit.

question: What does the letter 'B' stand for in the emergency ABCDE assessment framework?

options.A: Bone stability
options.B: Bleeding
options.C: Blood pressure
options.D: Breathing

explanation: In the standard emergency assessment framework, B stands for breathing, ensuring the patient is exchanging air adequately after the airway is cleared. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T2#GNS315_U1_T2_h2)

question: What do we call bacteria that have a round or spherical shape?

options.A: Bacilli
options.B: Hyphae
options.C: Spirilla
options.D: Cocci

explanation: Well done! Round bacteria are called cocci, while rod-shaped ones are bacilli. Think of 'cocci' as cozy little spheres!

question: Why do leprosy patients often end up with serious sores on their hands and feet?

options.A: Unbearable itching makes them scratch too hard
options.B: Blood completely stops flowing to the fingers and toes
options.C: Loss of feeling causes them to injure themselves without knowing
options.D: Bacteria directly dissolve the skin cells

explanation: Because they can't feel pain, heat, or sharp objects, minor cuts go unnoticed and turn into nasty ulcers. You're building solid clinical instincts!

question: Which of these is NOT a typical negative effect of widespread juvenile delinquency on society?

options.A: Destruction of public and private property
options.B: Surplus funding for educational infrastructure
options.C: Increased crime rates and community insecurity
options.D: Loss of productive human capital among youths

explanation: Well spotted! Delinquency drains money toward security and courts, so it definitely doesn't create extra funding for schools.

question: What is the employment status of a newly hired nurse who is still undergoing their initial probationary period?

options.A: Temporary or probationary pending formal confirmation
options.B: Employed strictly as an independent private contractor
options.C: Operating under an unverified volunteer agreement
options.D: Fully confirmed with permanent pensionable status

explanation: Every new civil servant starts out on probation. Once you prove yourself over time, your appointment gets fully confirmed!

question: What is the main goal of maternal home healthcare visits in our communities?

options.A: To bridge the gap between hospital services and community living
options.B: To distribute free prescription drugs to every household
options.C: To replace the need for hospital delivery entirely
options.D: To enforce strict hospital rules inside family compounds

explanation: Home visits let you bring health education and monitoring right to the doorstep of mothers who find it hard to visit the clinic regularly. You're making healthcare accessible where they live!

question: What electrical change happens inside the cell to spark a smell signal?

options.A: An influx of sodium and calcium ions into the cell
options.B: A sudden drop in cyclic AMP levels
options.C: The direct breakdown of protein molecules
options.D: A massive outflow of potassium ions

explanation: Correct! When ion channels open, positively charged sodium and calcium ions rush inside the cell. This change in electrical charge creates an impulse that travels up to the brain.

question: Why must you watch the baby closely with a CTG machine when giving an oxytocin drip?

options.A: Oxytocin makes the baby sleep deeply throughout the entire procedure.
options.B: Oxytocin causes the cervix to close up instead of opening further.
options.C: Oxytocin permanently lowers the mother's blood pressure to dangerous levels.
options.D: Oxytocin can cause uterine hyperstimulation, leading to reduced blood flow and fetal distress.

explanation: Spot on! Too much oxytocin can make contractions come too fast without resting breaks, cutting off oxygen to the baby. Safety first!

question: What happens to maternal bones if a breastfeeding mother does not consume enough calcium in her diet?

options.A: Her bones become significantly denser and stronger
options.B: Calcium is drawn from her bones to maintain milk quality
options.C: Her body stops producing milk until she takes supplements
options.D: Her breast milk becomes completely devoid of calcium

explanation: The body will take calcium from the mother's bones to ensure the baby's milk has what it needs if dietary intake falls short. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T009#GNS227_U2_T009_h4)

question: How do unequal gender roles in a relationship usually affect a woman's reproductive choices?

options.A: She may lack the authority to decide on contraceptive use or family size
options.B: She automatically gains complete control over household finances
options.C: Extended family members lose all interest in her personal life
options.D: Her partner is legally required to consult her on all medical matters

explanation: You got it! In male-dominated settings, women often struggle to make independent choices about birth control.

question: Why do deep scratches or infections on the cornea take so long to heal?

options.A: Sunlight constantly damages the cornea
options.B: Tears wash away all the healing white blood cells
options.C: The cornea does not have its own blood supply
options.D: Eye germs are immune to normal inflammation

explanation: Correct! Because the cornea has no blood vessels of its own, infection-fighting cells and nutrients have to travel a long way from nearby tissues, slowing down healing.

question: A patient has severe brain swelling, and you need a fluid that will draw excess water out of the swollen cells and back into the bloodstream. What type of IV solution do you need?

options.A: Hypoosmolar solution
options.B: Isotonic solution
options.C: Hypertonic solution
options.D: Hypotonic solution

explanation: You got it! Hypertonic fluids are concentrated, creating an osmotic pressure that pulls fluid out of tissue cells and safely back into the blood vessels.

question: What is the main reason body tissues get damaged once immune complexes settle in them?

options.A: Inflammation and enzyme release caused by white blood cells
options.B: Direct toxicity of the foreign serum on organ cells
options.C: Rapid multiplication of bacteria inside the trapped complexes
options.D: Complete blockage of oxygen supply to the major organs

explanation: Your white blood cells rush to help clear the mess, but their protective enzymes end up causing friendly fire on local tissues!

question: Which safety measure is especially crucial in adult day care centers serving clients with cognitive impairment or dementia?

options.A: Restricted visiting hours for family members only
options.B: Locked individual client bedrooms for overnight sleeping
options.C: Mandatory physical restraints for all mobile participants
options.D: Secure entry and exit points to prevent wandering

explanation: Because many participants experience confusion or memory loss, controlled exits are vital to prevent elopement and ensure client safety. [learn more](GNS324_U5_T7#GNS324_U5_T7_h8)

question: Which simple home modification helps prevent dangerous tripping hazards for someone using a walker?

options.A: Removing loose throw rugs from the floors
options.B: Adding decorative floor mats near doorways
options.C: Waxing hardwood floors until they shine
options.D: Placing heavy wooden furniture in hallways

explanation: Loose throw rugs easily bunch up under mobility aids like walkers and wheel tips, creating a major fall hazard. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T9#GNS225_U5_T9_h5)

question: A young woman who had FGM as a child comes to your clinic with painful periods and trouble passing urine. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: A newly developed hormonal imbalance
options.B: An acute bacterial kidney infection
options.C: Scar tissue buildup and urethral obstruction
options.D: Normal physiological changes of aging

explanation: Years of healing leave tough scar tissue that can block the urinary and vaginal openings, making both urination and menstruation very painful.

question: What is a common misconception people have about children with conduct disorders?

options.A: They are incapable of feeling physical pain
options.B: They never experience sadness
options.C: They always excel in mathematics
options.D: They always have low intelligence

explanation: Many people mistakenly assume these children have intellectual disabilities, but their cognitive capacity is usually right in the average range.

question: What is a main duty of an occupational health nurse working as a case manager?

options.A: Conducting annual financial audits for human resources
options.B: Designing new production machinery to eliminate safety hazards
options.C: Coordinating medical treatments and return-to-work plans for injured staff
options.D: Purchasing personal protective equipment for the entire industrial plant

explanation: Exactly! As case managers, nurses guide injured workers through their recovery and help them safely get back to work.

question: What does the term 'aging in place' mean for elderly patients?

options.A: Traveling across the country without any medical help
options.B: Staying in the emergency room for extended observation
options.C: Living safely in one's own home rather than a facility
options.D: Moving into a large hospital permanently

explanation: Aging in place refers to older adults remaining in their private residences while receiving needed support services. [learn more](GNS324_U1_T8#GNS324_U1_T8_h4)

question: Which common pregnancy complication is closely linked to widespread placental infarctions (tissue death)?

options.A: Gestational diabetes
options.B: Preeclampsia
options.C: Hyperemesis gravidarum
options.D: Iron deficiency anemia

explanation: High blood pressure disorders like preeclampsia narrow the tiny blood vessels in the placenta, cutting off proper blood flow and causing small areas of tissue to die. [learn more](GNS121_U6_T6#GNS121_U6_T6_h5)

question: What does the FIFO acronym stand for in food inventory management?

options.A: First-In, First-Out
options.B: Fast-Item, Fresh-Object
options.C: Fresh-Inspection, Final-Order
options.D: Freezer-Inside, Food-Out

explanation: FIFO means the items that arrived first are used first to prevent food from expiring on the shelf. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T012#GNS227_U3_T012_h7)

question: What usually happens to vulval varicose veins after the baby is born?

options.A: They immediately spread upward into the abdominal cavity
options.B: They always turn into permanent open ulcers on the skin
options.C: They remain unchanged for the rest of the woman's life
options.D: They shrink and regress significantly within a few weeks

explanation: Once delivery happens and hormone levels drop back down, the pelvic pressure disappears, and those swollen veins naturally shrink back down. Nature heals wonderfully!

question: What key stage of a parasite's life cycle happens inside its definitive host?

options.A: The parasite reaches maturity and reproduces sexually
options.B: The parasite dies off because the immune system is too strong
options.C: The parasite transforms directly into an ectoparasite
options.D: The parasite only undergoes brief larval resting stages

explanation: You're doing great! The definitive host is the VIP lounge for the parasite—it's where they finally grow up into adults and reproduce.

question: Why do hospitals carefully sort and classify different types of medical waste?

options.A: It ensures all hospital refuse can be buried together safely
options.B: It completely eliminates the need for any protective personal equipment
options.C: It reduces the volume of general waste produced by patients
options.D: It dictates the correct treatment and disposal method for each item type

explanation: You've got this! Different waste types need specific treatments, like incineration for body parts or autoclaving for lab equipment. Sorting helps us do it safely.

question: Under Herzberg's Two-Factor Theory, which of these is considered a basic 'hygiene factor'?

options.A: Opportunities for career advancement
options.B: Physical working conditions
options.C: Public recognition for good work
options.D: Personal sense of achievement

explanation: Hygiene factors are the basics of your work environment—like salary, job security, and good physical conditions. If they are missing, you get unhappy, but fixing them just brings you to neutral!

question: Why are art and creative therapies so helpful for trauma survivors?

options.A: They replace the need for professional psychiatric counseling
options.B: They completely cure post-traumatic stress disorder in one session
options.C: They allow expression of emotions that are hard to put into words
options.D: They force patients to relive painful memories out loud

explanation: Trauma can be really tough to talk about. Creative outlets like drawing or painting give patients a safe way to let those heavy feelings out.

question: What happens to disease prevalence if a new, highly effective cure is discovered?

options.A: Prevalence doubles because more people will seek testing
options.B: Prevalence increases because cured patients are counted twice
options.C: Prevalence stays the same because cures do not affect statistics
options.D: Prevalence decreases because patients recover and leave the active pool

explanation: Quick recovery removes people from the count of existing cases, driving the prevalence rate down. [learn more](GNS313_U1_T12#GNS313_U1_T12_h4)

question: A cook uses the same chopping board for raw chicken and fresh tomatoes without washing it first. What just happened?

options.A: Chemical toxicity
options.B: Physical adulteration
options.C: Cross-contamination
options.D: Thermal destruction

explanation: Using dirty equipment between raw meat and fresh veggies easily transfers bacteria from one to the other. Spot on!

question: What is the best way for a nurse leader to handle a transport breakdown during community outreach?

options.A: Wait passively until the government builds a paved highway
options.B: Blame the community members for living in a hard-to-reach area
options.C: Use adaptive problem-solving to find alternative transport methods
options.D: Cancel all future community outreach programs indefinitely

explanation: Great nurses are resourceful! When plans hit a roadblock, we think on our feet and find another way to reach our patients.

question: How is Ultra-High Temperature (UHT) milk different from standard pasteurized milk?

options.A: UHT milk contains chemical preservatives instead of heat treatment
options.B: UHT milk can remain shelf-stable at room temperature until opened

question: What is the double nutritional challenge facing the Nigerian healthcare system today?

options.A: Complete absence of nutritional disorders in urban and rural areas

options.C: Strictly overnutrition and obesity with no forms of hunger
options.D: Dealing with undernutrition while also seeing a rise in chronic lifestyle diseases

explanation: Nigeria faces a double burden: fighting traditional issues like hunger and malnutrition while also managing lifestyle illnesses like diabetes and high blood pressure.

question: A patient's heart rate is 42 beats per minute, and they feel dizzy with low blood pressure. Which emergency drug should the nurse expect to give?

options.A: Atropine
options.B: Metoprolol
options.C: Epinephrine
options.D: Digoxin

explanation: Atropine is the go-to emergency medication used to block vagal slowing and quickly bring up a dangerously low, symptomatic heart rate.

question: Which part of the small intestine connects directly to the stomach?

options.A: Jejunum
options.B: Cecum
options.C: Duodenum
options.D: Ileum

question: Where do most traditional drug administration abbreviations come from?

options.A: Ancient Greek literature
options.B: Latin terminology
options.C: Modern medical shorthand
options.D: French pharmaceutical guides

explanation: Great job! Most medical abbreviations are rooted in old Latin terms that doctors and pharmacists used historically to describe how drugs should be taken.

question: Why is keeping a buffer stock important for a clinical ward?

options.A: It gives staff extra items to sell to private individuals
options.B: It protects against unexpected patient surges and delivery delays
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for an inventory ledger
options.D: It ensures that drugs never expire while sitting on the shelf

explanation: Think of buffer stock as your safety cushion. It saves the day when patient admissions spike suddenly or delivery trucks run late.

question: Why do we ask patients to take off all jewelry and metallic objects before an X-ray?

options.A: They make the patient feel too heavy on the table
options.B: They attract stray electrical currents from the machine
options.C: They cause the X-ray tube to overheat quickly

question: A patient has a long-standing infection that cuts down blood supply, making the affected cells shrink. What is this adaptation called?

options.A: Hyperplasia
options.B: Atrophy
options.C: Hypertrophy
options.D: Metaplasia

explanation: Atrophy is when cells shrink and get smaller due to less work, poor blood supply, or chronic illness. Think of it as cells downsizing!

question: How do we best describe substance intoxication in clinical practice?

options.A: A mild nutritional deficiency resulting from poor diet
options.B: A permanent physical injury caused by chemical toxicity
options.C: A temporary, reversible impairment of mental and physical function
options.D: A lifelong genetic disorder of the central nervous system

explanation: You nailed it! Intoxication is a short-term, reversible state that happens right after someone takes a psychoactive substance. It passes as the body clears the drug.

question: What is the main goal of using healthcare simulation in nursing education?

options.A: To safely bridge classroom theory with clinical practice
options.B: To replace traditional classroom lectures completely
options.C: To reduce the number of hours spent in real hospitals
options.D: To test students so they can be ranked in their class

explanation: Simulation gives students a bridge between what they read in books and the realities of caring for patients, all without any risk of harm. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T8#GNS212_U4_T8_h1)

question: How can poorly tied or weak waste bags lead to new infections for patients?

options.A: By reducing the overall humidity levels required for bacterial survival

options.C: By directly increasing the room temperature of the clinical ward

question: What is the best nursing action when you spot a potential drug interaction on a patient's chart?

options.A: Administer the medications at the exact same time to save nursing time

options.C: Stop all of the patient's home medications permanently without telling anyone

question: Which food group is most helpful to prevent constipation in older adults who aren't very active?

options.A: Simple sugars
options.B: Animal proteins
options.C: Dietary fiber
options.D: Saturated fats

explanation: Great thinking! Fiber adds bulk to stool and keeps things moving smoothly, helping make up for slower digestion in older age.

question: What factor has the biggest influence on the overall survival outlook for a patient with a vulval tumour?

options.A: The stage of the cancer at the time of diagnosis
options.B: The specific brand of dressing used on the wound
options.C: The patient's personal preference for radiation therapy
options.D: The exact age of the patient during surgery

explanation: Well done! Catching the cancer early, before it spreads to the lymph nodes, gives the patient the best chance at long-term survival.

question: Which test is most important to confirm that syphilis has reached the brain?

options.A: Lumbar puncture to check the cerebrospinal fluid
options.B: A full-body CT scan
options.C: An EEG to check brain waves
options.D: Routine urinalysis and urine culture

question: A nurse is teaching a patient how to do Kegel exercises correctly. What is the key instruction?

options.A: Contract the pelvic floor muscles as if trying to stop the flow of urine
options.B: Squeeze the abdominal and thigh muscles tightly while holding your breath
options.C: Push down gently as if having a bowel movement
options.D: Flex the buttocks and hips until your pelvis rises off the bed

question: What can happen if severe, constant pregnancy heartburn is left completely untreated?

options.A: Inflammation and damage to the lining of the esophagus

question: Why are visual aids and practical demonstrations useful during health counseling in primary care?

options.A: They replace the need for the nurse to speak at all
options.B: They make health messages easier to understand for people with varying literacy levels
options.C: They ensure patients never forget a single word of advice
options.D: They make the clinic look more modern and well-equipped

explanation: Visuals and demonstrations bridge literacy gaps and make abstract health concepts concrete and memorable. [learn more](GNS124_U5_T12#GNS124_U5_T12_h6)

question: Where do T-lymphocytes go to mature?

options.A: Spleen
options.B: Bone marrow

options.D: Thymus

question: What is a major problem when writing infection control policies?

options.A: Making them too long and complicated for busy staff to use
options.B: Writing them in English instead of the local native language
options.C: Printing them on paper instead of viewing them on a mobile phone
options.D: Including pictures of medical equipment that look too modern

explanation: Exactly! If a policy is too heavy and academic, busy nurses on a tense shift won't have time to read it.

question: How does early substance abuse affect the brain's natural reward system?

options.A: It alters pathways so normal activities no longer bring pleasure
options.B: It stops the brain from producing any blood flow
options.C: It makes normal daily activities feel intensely rewarding
options.D: It permanently repairs damaged nerve cells in the brain

question: What does resource mobilization mean during a disaster?

options.A: Firing healthcare workers who fail to report to duty during crises
options.B: Gathering funds, supplies, and equipment from diverse partners and donors
options.C: Exporting local medical equipment to wealthier neighboring countries

explanation: Resource mobilization is simply pulling together all the money, materials, and help needed from different partners.

question: What is the best way to learn about a family's cultural or religious death traditions?

options.A: Ignore cultural practices to maintain strict hospital routines
options.B: Ask open-ended questions to learn about their specific preferences
options.C: Insist that hospital customs always override personal traditions
options.D: Assume all families from the same country share identical beliefs

explanation: Never assume! Always ask open, respectful questions so you can learn what matters most to that specific family.

question: When a patient has 'dysphagia', what exact trouble are they experiencing?

options.A: Frequent vomiting
options.B: Severe stomach pain
options.C: Involuntary weight loss
options.D: Difficulty swallowing

question: On a quality improvement team, what is the data analyst's main job?

options.A: Resolves personal conflicts between staff members
options.B: Leads bedside patient care procedures every shift
options.C: Runs team meetings and keeps the group focused

explanation: You got it! The data analyst looks at the numbers and metrics to check progress and prove whether a new change is actually making things better.

question: What is the correct way to store an epinephrine auto-injector?

options.A: Leave it inside a parked car during hot sunny days for easy access.
options.B: Store it tightly sealed inside the kitchen refrigerator to preserve potency.

options.D: Keep it at room temperature and protect it from extreme heat and light.

question: How does a shortage of nursing staff directly impact patient care in a hospital?

options.A: It reduces patient waiting times in the emergency room.

options.C: It automatically improves the quality of surgical procedures.
options.D: It ensures that every patient gets private room nursing.

question: An elderly patient with arthritis uses a walking frame, but their small room is packed with heavy furniture. What should you do first?

options.A: Instruct the patient to stop using the walker immediately
options.B: Report the housing conditions to local law enforcement
options.C: Advise the patient to move to a skilled nursing facility today
options.D: Help rearrange and clear pathways to allow safe walker passage

question: What primary category of life does water microbiology study?

options.B: Microscopic organisms found in water
options.C: Large aquatic plants and fish
options.D: Mineral deposits in borehole pipes

question: What is the best next step for a patient who comes back with a strongly positive Mantoux test?

options.A: Discharge the patient with instructions to return next year
options.B: Refer the patient for a chest X-ray and clinical evaluation
options.C: Immediately start a full course of multi-drug TB treatment
options.D: Administer a second booster Mantoux test on the other arm

explanation: A positive skin test is a warning sign, not a final diagnosis. We always send them for a chest X-ray to check if their lungs are clear or if the infection is active. [learn more](GNS213_U5_T12#GNS213_U5_T12_h8)

question: What is the main goal of mitigation in disaster management?

options.A: To provide immediate medical care during a crisis
options.B: To reduce the severity of potential hazards
options.C: To conduct evacuation drills right before a storm
options.D: To rebuild homes after a disaster has occurred

explanation: Mitigation is all about taking action *before* a disaster strikes to lessen its blow on people and property. Think of it as putting up strong safeguards early! [learn more](GNS315_U1_T9#GNS315_U1_T9_h1)

question: Which group of people faces the highest risk of severe complications from food contamination?

options.A: Young adults with desk jobs
options.B: Teenagers playing sports
options.C: Young children and the elderly
options.D: Healthy middle-aged workers

explanation: Very young children and older adults have weaker immune systems, making it much harder for their bodies to fight off food poisoning. [learn more](GNS227_U3_T012#GNS227_U3_T012_h1)

question: What is the main goal of good nutrition in Primary Health Care (PHC)?

options.A: Replacing clinical treatments with herbal remedies
options.B: Preventing deficiency diseases and supporting optimal potential
options.C: Eliminating the need for agricultural market regulations
options.D: Reducing the cost of commercial food imports

explanation: You got this! In PHC, good nutrition is all about helping people stay healthy, avoiding illness, and reaching their full body and mind development. Keep it up!

question: Which layer of cells in the early embryo develops into the nervous system?

options.A: Mesoderm
options.B: Epiblast
options.C: Ectoderm
options.D: Endoderm

explanation: You got this! The ectoderm is the outermost layer of the early embryo. It forms the neural plate, which builds our amazing nervous system.

question: Why do nurses prefer using large-bore IV catheters when handling emergency resuscitation?

options.A: They allow rapid infusion of fluids and emergency drugs
options.B: They can remain inside the vein for up to two weeks safely
options.C: They prevent the need to monitor blood pressure regularly
options.D: They cause less pain when inserted into small arm veins

explanation: A wider tube means fluids can rush in much faster to save a crashing patient. Smart thinking!

question: Why is it so important to include family caregivers when teaching patients home care?

options.A: To teach them how to prescribe changes in physical therapy exercises
options.B: To train them to perform minor orthopedic surgeries at home
options.C: To legally transfer full medical responsibility of the client to them
options.D: To ensure they know how to support safe movement and spot warning signs

explanation: Exactly! Family members are the main helpers at home, so teaching them helps keep the patient safe and catches problems early.

question: What action should happen immediately after the baby is born and dried?

options.A: Washing the baby with the kit soap
options.B: Weighing the baby on a scale
options.C: Giving the mother oral pain medicine
options.D: Tying and cutting the umbilical cord

explanation: Once the baby is delivered and initial drying and assessment take place, managing the umbilical cord safely is the next vital step. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T10#GNS225_U2_T10_h4)

question: Which nursing action is an example of secondary prevention?

options.A: Running a stress-reduction workshop for healthy adults
options.B: Screening high school students for early signs of depression
options.C: Administering emergency life support for a drug overdose
options.D: Providing long-term rehabilitation for chronic schizophrenia

explanation: Secondary prevention focuses on early detection and prompt treatment to stop mild symptoms from becoming severe disorders. [learn more](GNS314_U5_T1#GNS314_U5_T1_h2)

question: Which animal is the main reservoir responsible for spreading the Lassa virus to humans?

options.A: Stray cats
options.B: Domestic dogs
options.C: Pigs and swine
options.D: Multimammate rats

explanation: You got it! Lassa fever is mainly passed to humans through contact with the urine and droppings of infected multimammate rats.

question: Which of the following actions is NOT safe practice when managing cardiac monitor alarms?

options.A: Checking the patient immediately whenever an alarm sounds
options.B: Customizing alarm limits to match the patient's baseline condition
options.C: Permanently disabling noisy alarms so staff can rest
options.D: Changing electrode pads regularly to protect the skin

explanation: Permanently turning off or ignoring alarms puts patients at severe risk if a real emergency occurs. [learn more](GNS212_U4_T2#GNS212_U4_T2_h6)

question: Why do nurses refer to pain as the 'fifth vital sign'?

options.A: It directly calculates the exact heart rate of the patient.
options.B: It can be measured using an automated cuff machine.
options.C: It must be checked and recorded alongside standard vital signs.
options.D: It is only relevant during surgical procedures.

explanation: Calling pain the fifth vital sign reminds us to assess and document it just as regularly as temperature or blood pressure. Great job keeping your clinical habits sharp!

question: Why is it important to discuss proper medication storage during counselling?

options.A: Heat and moisture can break down drug potency
options.B: Expired pills turn into nutritional supplements
options.C: Refrigeration doubles the active dose strength
options.D: Plastic bottles attract dangerous insects

explanation: Improper storage in humid or hot places like bathrooms can ruin the chemical stability of medications. [learn more](GNS215_U4_T7#GNS215_U4_T7_h4)

question: Why is delegation such a helpful skill for nurses on a busy ward?

options.A: It allows nurses to manage workload by sharing routine care tasks safely
options.B: It prevents junior staff from learning advanced clinical procedures
options.C: It eliminates the need for any direct patient assessment by the nurse
options.D: It completely removes nursing liability from ward management

explanation: Delegation isn't about passing the buck; it's about teamwork! It helps spread out daily care duties so every patient gets timely attention.

question: How do illegal buildings put over drainage channels affect urban flooding?

options.A: They improve the response time of ambulances during storms
options.B: They worsen urban flooding by blocking the natural flow of water
options.C: They provide safe temporary shelters for displaced families
options.D: They serve as command centers for emergency rescue teams

explanation: When waterways are blocked by construction, rainwater has nowhere to go, causing heavy and destructive floods in the city. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T9#GNS315_U1_T9_h7)

question: Besides keeping the skin clean, what is a key benefit of bathing a bedridden patient?

options.A: Preventing the patient from ever developing a fever
options.B: Completely eliminating the need for any pain medication
options.C: Stimulating blood circulation and assessing skin integrity
options.D: Lowering the patient's blood pressure permanently

explanation: Great job thinking clinically! Moving the skin and tissues gently during a bath boosts blood flow and gives you a wonderful chance to spot early signs of bedsores.

question: Why is clear teamwork and role assignment so vital on an evacuation mission?

options.A: Cramped spaces and high-stress environments require smooth teamwork
options.B: Patients feel anxious when roles overlap during transit
options.C: Aircraft weight limits change based on who is performing procedures
options.D: Hospital regulations fine teams that overlap their clinical duties

explanation: When space is tight and time is ticking, everyone needs to know their exact job so the team can work like a well-oiled machine without getting in each other's way.

question: Which of these items belongs specifically in the pathological waste category?

options.A: An empty bottle of paracetamol syrup
options.B: A cardboard box used for office files
options.C: A discarded plastic wrapper from a sterile syringe
options.D: An amputated human limb from the surgical theatre

explanation: Spot on! Pathological waste refers to human tissues, organs, and body parts removed during surgeries or autopsies. You've got this!

question: A nursing mother complains of extreme fatigue and a noticeable drop in milk supply after starting a very strict, low-calorie weight loss diet. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Inadequate daily caloric intake to support milk synthesis
options.B: A sudden hormonal imbalance unrelated to her food intake
options.C: Normal physiological changes that happen at three months postpartum
options.D: Drinking too much plain water instead of sugary beverages

explanation: Drastic calorie restriction robs the body of the energy required to make milk, leading to fatigue and reduced supply. [learn more](GNS227_U2_T009#GNS227_U2_T009_h2)

question: Why does a community nurse look at the whole household instead of just one sick person?

options.A: Diseases always hit every family member at the exact same second
options.B: National insurance only pays for whole households
options.C: Hospital rules ban treating single patients alone
options.D: Family members share the same living conditions, risks, and environment

explanation: Brilliant! Since family members eat from the same pot and live under the same roof, a health risk or crisis usually affects everyone in the home.

question: How often are hospital policies typically scheduled for review and updating?

options.A: Every two to three years
options.B: Every twenty to thirty years
options.C: Only after a major court case occurs
options.D: Every single week without fail

explanation: Policies are checked every few years to keep up with new medical evidence, changing laws, and real feedback from the wards.

question: A patient with high blood pressure and high blood sugar is told to switch from white bread to whole grain bread. Why is this a great choice?

options.A: Refined white bread has no calories for the body to process
options.B: Whole grains retain fiber, which slows digestion and prevents sharp sugar spikes
options.C: Whole grains eliminate all fats from the patient's daily diet
options.D: Whole grains contain complete proteins that repair damaged blood vessels

explanation: You nailed it! The natural fiber in whole grains slows down how fast sugar enters the blood, keeping levels nice and steady.

question: A patient wants to eat more fiber without getting severe gas and bloating. What advice should you give?

options.A: Introduce high-fiber foods slowly so the digestive system can adapt over time.
options.B: Take strong laxatives with every single meal containing fiber.
options.C: Stop eating all forms of fiber completely to avoid any digestive effort.
options.D: Eat a massive amount of beans and raw vegetables all at once on day one.

explanation: Slow and steady wins the race! Giving the gut time to adjust to fiber prevents sudden cramps and gas.

question: When a nurse scans a patient's medication barcode, which step of the computer cycle is happening?

options.A: Processing
options.B: Storage
options.C: Output
options.D: Input

explanation: Whenever you type, click, or scan something into the computer, you are giving it 'input'. Great job!

question: You are getting ready to put a new colostomy bag on a patient. What is the right first step for the skin?

options.A: Rub a thick layer of oily moisturizing lotion to soften the skin
options.B: Scrub the area hard with an alcohol-based antiseptic
options.C: Dust the moist skin heavily with a scented powder
options.D: Clean the skin gently with warm water and pat it completely dry

explanation: Correct! The skin needs to be clean and totally dry so the adhesive barrier can stick securely without leaking.

question: Why are group therapy sessions used so much in day hospitals?

options.A: They help build social skills and provide peer support
options.B: They reduce the number of staff members needed on duty
options.C: They are required by law for all nursing documentation
options.D: They eliminate the need for individual psychiatric evaluation

explanation: You're right! Groups give patients a safe space to practice talking with others and learn from shared experiences.

question: Which part of the pelvis serves as the actual passageway for a baby during birth?

options.A: True pelvis
options.B: Ilioc fossa
options.C: Abdominal cavity
options.D: False pelvis

question: What is the main difference between a mild Grade I sprain and a severe Grade III sprain?

options.A: Grade III involves complete ligament rupture and joint instability
options.B: Grade I presents with immediate inability to bear weight
options.C: Grade III only causes microscopic tearing of fibers
options.D: Grade I always requires surgical correction

explanation: A Grade I sprain is just a mild stretch with a steady joint. A Grade III sprain means the ligament is completely torn, leading to a wobbly, unstable joint.

question: When checking a home for safety, which of these is a common physical hazard?

options.A: High white blood cell count
options.B: Elevated resting heart rate
options.C: Incorrect medication dosage
options.D: Loose floor rugs

explanation: Watch out for loose rugs! They are physical hazards that easily cause elderly patients to trip and fall at home.

question: What is the safest way to handle a deceased patient's jewelry and cash?

options.A: Document them and hand them to family or hospital administration
options.B: Send them along with the body directly to the mortuary
options.C: Give them to the ward cleaner for safekeeping
options.D: Leave them securely locked inside the bedside drawer

explanation: Valuables must be formally documented and given to the family or administrative authorities to prevent loss or theft. [learn more](GNS221_U4_T10#GNS221_U4_T10_h5)

question: What simple administrative step helps stop children from disappearing into trafficking rings?

options.A: Banning travel between states
options.B: Mandatory military service
options.C: Closing local primary schools
options.D: Universal birth registration

explanation: Official birth records give a child a legal identity, making it much harder for traffickers to move them around unnoticed.

question: Why is keeping enough potassium inside the cells so crucial for your patients?

options.A: It directly controls blood pressure in the arteries
options.B: It prevents the kidneys from producing too much urine
options.C: It regulates red blood cell production in bone marrow
options.D: It maintains stable heart rhythm and muscle action

explanation: Exactly! Potassium is a heart-loving electrolyte. When potassium levels go out of whack, the heart and muscles can struggle to beat properly.

question: Which of the following is NOT a good way to protect external validity in clinical research?

options.A: Testing patients only in a hidden laboratory with strict artificial rules
options.B: Conducting the study across multiple different hospitals
options.C: Including patients of various ages and backgrounds
options.D: Using a sample of participants that represents the real patient population

question: Which of these can act as a reservoir where germs live?

options.A: Completely dry and sunny metal surfaces
options.B: Sterile surgical instruments only
options.C: Soil, water, humans, and animals
options.D: Intact human skin with no normal flora

explanation: Germs aren't picky! They can live inside living hosts like humans and animals, or in the environment like soil and water.

question: Why is it a bad idea to put a hot water bottle on a patient's brand-new swelling?

options.A: It hardens the skin into a permanent scar
options.B: It stops all heart function and lowers blood pressure
options.C: It increases blood flow and can make the swelling worse
options.D: It immediately causes permanent skin freezing

question: Which of these is NOT a typical side effect of immune checkpoint inhibitors?

options.C: Permanent structural damage to the heart muscle valves
options.D: Dermatitis and itchy rashes across the skin surface

question: What assisted reproductive technique involves injecting a single sperm directly into an egg?

options.A: Intracytoplasmic sperm injection
options.B: Vasectomy reversal
options.C: In vitro fertilization
options.D: Intrauterine insemination

question: A village is turning down a new immunization drive because of heavy rumors. What should you do first?

options.A: Ignore the rumors and continue vaccinating those who show up voluntarily
options.B: Engage trusted community leaders and local influencers to discuss concerns
options.C: Report the community to security forces for refusing public health care

explanation: Exactly! Working through respected local figures is the best way to clear up misunderstandings, answer questions, and build genuine trust.

question: How do strict cultural and religious beliefs usually impact a young woman facing an unintended pregnancy?

options.A: They eliminate the need for any form of healthcare
options.B: They automatically provide financial support for single mothers
options.C: They increase the social pressure to carry the pregnancy to term
options.D: They encourage open dialogue between family members

question: A woman's last menstrual period began on January 1st. Using Naegele's rule, what is her estimated date of delivery (EDD)?

options.A: September 15th

options.C: October 8th
options.D: December 25th

question: Which pulse site is standard for checking a routine heart rate in a conscious adult patient?

options.A: Popliteal pulse
options.B: Radial pulse
options.C: Apical pulse
options.D: Carotid pulse

question: What does the term 'attrition' mean in longitudinal research?

options.B: The process of cleaning data in a computer spreadsheet

question: Which medication class is well known for increasing blood sugar levels during therapy?

options.A: Laxatives

question: In radiation safety, what does the golden rule acronym 'ALARA' stand for?

options.A: Always Limit All Radiologic Assessments

options.C: Avoid Lower Area Radiation Accidents
options.D: As Low As Reasonably Achievable

question: A community nurse visits a patient with psychosis who looks very suspicious and guarded. What is the best first move?

explanation: Brilliant! Taking it slow and building a friendly rapport helps lower anxiety so the patient feels safe enough to talk.

question: Why is it so important to tell a patient to cough up deep lung mucus instead of just spitting out mouth saliva for a TB test?

question: Which part of an antibody molecule binds directly to a specific antigen?

question: Why do we teach mothers to recognize danger signs in their babies during clinic visits?

options.C: To prevent them from consulting traditional healers ever

question: Why is careful documentation and evidence preservation important when treating a suspected assault?

question: A community health nurse sets up a free blood sugar screening in the market. What level of prevention is this?

options.D: Universal prevention

question: Which tool is specifically used to check a patient's risk of falling?

question: Which of the following is a common barrier to effective family planning referrals in Nigeria?

question: Why is it important to conduct nursing research right here in Nigeria instead of relying only on foreign studies?

question: What is the main goal of safe motherhood initiatives?

question: In the popular SBAR communication tool used by healthcare workers, what does the letter 'B' stand for?

question: Which of these is NOT a good practice when validating your clinic's data?

question: What is the primary role of traditional and religious leaders in policy implementation?

question: Why do people naturally perform the Valsalva maneuver (bearing down) when passing stool?

question: How do bad roads and insecurity impact the work of voluntary health agencies?

question: A senior doctor frequently interrupts junior nurses and dominates a committee meeting. What is the best action for the chairperson to take?

question: What is the primary focus of Prong 2 in the WHO PMTCT strategy?

question: When did the World Health Organization (WHO) publish its first Model List of Essential Medicines?

question: What is the main goal of routine health check-ups in the workplace?

question: Which type of infection control precautions must you practice with every single patient you care for?

question: Which type of shock is caused by a massive loss of blood or body fluids?

question: Which specific brain cells are mainly destroyed in Parkinson's disease?

question: Which of these is NOT a challenge when trying to provide mental health care in primary clinics?

question: What is a major benefit of tele-health for patients living far away from city hospitals?

question: What should a nursing unit manager do immediately after setting targets with the staff?

question: A patient with a broken arm can walk around and is breathing fine. What triage color do they get?

question: Which of these is NOT a sign of a dangerous, severe allergic reaction to contrast dye?
