options.D: Swelling of the lips and tongue

explanation: A metallic taste is totally normal! Hives, swollen lips, and trouble breathing, however, are red flags that mean we need to act fast.

question: Why should families pick a specific meeting place outside their home when planning for emergencies?

options.A: To ensure everyone can reunite safely if separated during an evacuation
options.B: To provide a storage space for heavy rescue tools
options.C: To serve as a temporary community clinic
options.D: To give neighbors a place to park their vehicles

explanation: Brilliant! Having a pre-arranged meeting spot saves precious time and stops panic if family members get separated during a sudden crisis.

question: What is usually the very first sign of leprosy on the skin?

options.A: A discolored patch that feels numb or less sensitive
options.B: Tiny water blisters on the hands
options.C: Painful open sores on the legs
options.D: Severe itching all over the body

explanation: A pale or reddish skin patch that doesn't feel normal touch or temperature is the classic early warning sign. Keep shining!

question: What is the primary maternal health benefit of properly spacing pregnancies?

options.A: Permanently stopping all future menstrual cycles
options.B: Eliminating the need for any antenatal care visits
options.C: Giving the mother's body time to recover physically
options.D: Ensuring the mother gives birth only to male children

explanation: Proper spacing allows a woman's body to restore vital nutrients like iron and heal from the physical stress of a previous pregnancy. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T002#GNS226_U6_T002_h1)

question: About how long does it take for a Guinea worm to mature and show up after someone drinks contaminated water?

options.A: Roughly one year
options.B: One to two weeks
options.C: About one month
options.D: Five to ten years

explanation: That's right! It's a slow journey—it usually takes about 10 to 14 months for the worm to grow inside the body before it tries to come out. Patience is key in nursing and in learning!

question: Why is the time spent bathing a patient so great for building the nurse-patient relationship?

options.A: It forces the patient to follow every single hospital rule without arguing
options.B: It gives the patient a chance to voice hidden fears and ask questions
options.C: It allows the nurse to complete all nursing documentation for the shift
options.D: It proves to the doctor that the nurse can complete physical tasks quickly

explanation: Spot on! That quiet, one-on-one time makes patients feel safe and cared for, often opening up about worries they wouldn't share in a busy hallway.

question: Which piece of equipment do you need to safely connect an oxygen mask to a hospital wall supply?

options.A: Sphygmomanometer
options.B: Suction canister
options.C: Flowmeter
options.D: Glucometer strip

explanation: The flowmeter plugs into the wall outlet so you can easily control and measure the liters per minute flowing to the patient.

question: What is a major risk for patients taking immune checkpoint inhibitors (immunotherapy)?

options.A: The medication causes immediate permanent sterility in both male and female patients.
options.B: The boosted immune system may attack normal, healthy organs, causing widespread inflammation.
options.C: The drug destroys bone marrow production completely, requiring lifelong platelet transfusions.
options.D: The patient will instantly lose all hair follicles within forty-eight hours of the first dose.

explanation: You got it! Reviving the immune system is great for fighting cancer, but sometimes the revved-up immune cells accidentally attack healthy organs like the lungs or gut.

question: What is the main job of Langerhans cells in the skin?

options.A: Sensing cold temperatures and gentle touches
options.B: Producing oily sebum to keep the skin soft and waterproof
options.C: Making the dark pigment that shields against sunlight
options.D: Catching and processing foreign invaders for the immune system

explanation: You got it! Langerhans cells are like security guards in the skin—they catch microbes and run to the lymph nodes to sound the alarm. [learn more](GNS211_U2_T3#GNS211_U2_T3_h4)

question: You walk into a patient's room who has a new tracheostomy and notice thick green discharge and redness around the hole (stoma). What should you suspect?

options.A: Normal healing process
options.B: Accidental tube decannulation
options.C: A local stoma infection
options.D: Over-inflation of the cuff

explanation: Green, pus-like discharge and redness are classic warning signs of a bacterial infection at the site. Always report this and keep the area clean!

question: When a nurse looks at an established hospital policy, what legal benchmark does it help define?

options.A: The standard of care expected of a prudent nurse
options.B: The total number of hours a nurse must sleep
options.C: The exact salary scale for different nursing ranks
options.D: The personal liability insurance cost per year

explanation: Courts look at hospital policies to figure out what a reasonably careful, well-trained nurse would have done in that exact clinical situation.

question: What is the general rule for how women with vulval varicose veins give birth?

options.A: A scheduled caesarean section is required in every single case
options.B: Labor must be induced early at thirty-six weeks gestation
options.C: Vaginal delivery is usually safe and successful for most women
options.D: Forceps delivery must be used to protect the perineal blood vessels

explanation: Good news! Having vulval varicosities doesn't automatically mean a C-section. Most mothers have safe, normal vaginal deliveries with proper supportive care.

question: What does checking a client's orientation involve during a mental status check?

options.A: Measuring the daily fluid intake and output
options.B: Testing physical muscle strength in the legs
options.C: Asking about person, place, and time
options.D: Checking hearing ability with a tuning fork

explanation: Orientation checks confirm if the client knows who they are, where they are located, and what time or date it is. [learn more](GNS222_U3_T5#GNS222_U3_T5_h4)

question: Why is proper sampling important when conducting a descriptive survey in a hospital?

options.A: It guarantees that every single patient in the country will be cured
options.B: It removes the need to analyze numerical data at the end
options.C: It stops patients from answering survey questions incorrectly
options.D: It ensures the selected group accurately reflects the entire patient population

explanation: Good sampling means the few people you study are a true mini-version of the whole group, making your findings reliable. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T9#GNS224_U1_T9_h5)

question: What does the null hypothesis usually say in a Chi-Square test of independence?

options.A: There is a strong positive correlation between variables
options.B: The observed frequencies equal zero
options.C: The sample size is too small to analyze
options.D: There is no association between the variables

explanation: That's right! The null hypothesis always starts by assuming there is no relationship between the things we are studying—any pattern we see is just by chance.

question: A grand multiparous woman arrives at the labor ward in active labor. What is the very first priority action you should take as the nurse?

options.A: Instruct the patient to push forcefully with every contraction
options.B: Set up an IV line and take blood for crossmatching
options.C: Prepare the patient for an immediate routine cesarean section
options.D: Administer general anesthesia to prevent any labor pain

explanation: Since heavy bleeding is a major risk for her, getting an IV line ready and having matched blood on standby before things get complicated is a true lifesaver.

question: An elderly patient has a weakened cough reflex. What major complication are they at risk for?

options.A: Sudden enlargement of the vocal cords
options.B: Spontaneous rupture of the diaphragm
options.C: Lower respiratory tract infections
options.D: Complete collapse of the nasal passages

explanation: Spot on! When older adults can't cough well, mucus stays trapped in the airways, becoming a breeding ground for bacteria and leading to chest infections.

question: What type of consent is assumed when an unconscious trauma patient requires immediate life-saving care?

options.A: Implied consent
options.B: Proxy consent
options.C: Informed consent
options.D: Written consent

explanation: Implied consent legally allows healthcare providers to treat unconscious emergency patients when asking permission is impossible. [learn more](GNS315_U1_T1#GNS315_U1_T1_h6)

question: Why is teaching such a huge part of a home health nurse's job?

options.A: Nurses are not allowed to perform hands-on procedures in homes
options.B: Home care agencies lack the budget for direct patient care
options.C: Physicians forbid nurses from making independent clinical decisions
options.D: Patients and families must manage daily safety when the nurse is gone

explanation: You only visit occasionally! Empowering the patient and their family with good safety habits is key to keeping them safe between your visits.

question: A patient with thick mucus cannot clear their throat and shows signs of airway blockage. What immediate nursing action is required?

options.A: Asking the patient to hold their breath for one minute
options.B: Placing the patient flat on their back to rest
options.C: Suctioning the airway to remove the trapped secretions
options.D: Administering a dose of blood pressure medication

explanation: When a patient cannot cough up mucus blocking their airway, suctioning physically clears the passage so air can flow. [learn more](GNS212_U2_T4#GNS212_U2_T4_h4)

question: Why would a doctor order a tympanometry test?

options.A: To test the patient's balance and coordination
options.B: To check middle ear function and detect fluid
options.C: To measure the electrical activity of the brain
options.D: To visualize the tiny bones of the inner ear directly

explanation: Tympanometry tests how well your eardrum moves when air pressure changes. It's great for spotting fluid or pressure issues behind the eardrum.

question: Why do community health nurses need to know basic epidemiological terms?

options.A: To diagnose rare surgical conditions in the emergency room
options.B: To track illnesses and plan local health outreaches effectively
options.C: To calculate hospital building construction costs
options.D: To prescribe complex medications without consulting doctors

explanation: Spotting disease trends helps you plan amazing, targeted health outreaches for your community. You're building skills that save real lives!

question: Administering post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) to a recent survivor of sexual assault falls under which level of prevention?

options.A: Tertiary prevention
options.B: Quaternary prevention
options.C: Secondary prevention
options.D: Primary prevention

explanation: Secondary prevention involves immediate medical interventions after exposure to prevent long-term harm like disease transmission. [learn more](GNS312_U4_T12#GNS312_U4_T12_h4)

question: Why can't nurses rely on regular surgical masks when caring for patients with airborne diseases?

options.A: Surgical masks trap moisture and destroy bacterial filters
options.B: Pathogens are small enough to pass through regular mask material
options.C: Droplet nuclei can easily bypass loose-fitting surgical masks
options.D: Surgical masks only protect against blood splashes

explanation: You've got this! Regular surgical masks aren't tightly sealed enough around the edges, meaning those sneaky floating droplet nuclei can slip right past them.

question: What is the absolute first thing to check and manage when a patient is brought in with a suspected drug overdose?

options.A: Drawing blood for lab tests
options.B: Finding out the exact name of the drug taken
options.C: Administering activated charcoal orally
options.D: Securing the airway, breathing, and circulation

explanation: You've got this! Always remember the ABCs (Airway, Breathing, Circulation) come first in any emergency. We keep the patient alive and breathing before we worry about detective work or giving specific medications.

question: Which simple tool does a community health nurse use to listen to the baby's heartbeat during a home visit?

options.A: A sphygmomanometer
options.B: An ophthalmoscope
options.C: A percussion hammer
options.D: A Pinard stethoscope

explanation: A Pinard stethoscope (or portable Doppler) is your trusty companion in the field for checking fetal heart tones!

question: Which member of the palliative team usually helps families navigate money troubles and community resources?

options.A: Social worker
options.B: Pharmacist
options.C: Surgeon
options.D: Physical therapist

explanation: You're right! Palliative social workers are lifesavers when it comes to connecting families with financial aid, support groups, and community resources.

question: A patient in a disaster zone has a severe head injury, is unresponsive, breathing irregularly, and has no pulse. Which triage category fits best?

options.A: Red
options.B: Black
options.C: Yellow
options.D: Green

explanation: You're doing great. A black tag (or expectant) is used for catastrophic injuries where survival is sadly very unlikely, helping us save resources for those we can help.

question: Why does staff resistance to change pose a major challenge to implementing a new ward plan?

options.A: Because it automatically increases the hospital annual financial budget
options.B: Because it forces managers to delete all previous institutional policies
options.C: Because nurses may refuse to adopt the new procedures, causing the plan to fail
options.D: Because it immediately stops all emergency patient admissions

explanation: If staff push back and refuse to cooperate with new routines, even the best-designed plan will fail in practice. [learn more](GST321_U1_T5#GST321_U1_T5_h6)

question: If a patient has an infection causing nausea, vomiting, and watery stool, what is the most important thing to watch out for?

options.A: Sudden muscle hypertrophy
options.B: Elevated blood pressure
options.C: Fluid volume deficit
options.D: High red blood cell count

explanation: Exactly right! Vomiting and diarrhea drain body fluids fast, putting the patient at high risk for dehydration.

question: If a patient gets infected through a mosquito bite, what type of transmission is this?

options.A: Feco-oral route
options.B: Vector-borne transmission
options.C: Direct skin penetration
options.D: Congenital transmission

explanation: Easy peasy! A 'vector' is like a living taxi (like a mosquito) that carries the parasite from one person to another.

question: What dangerous habit must nurses watch out for when patients use axillary crutches?

options.A: Resting body weight directly on the armpits
options.B: Looking straight ahead instead of down at the floor
options.C: Holding the handgrips too loosely with the palms
options.D: Walking too slowly during hallway exercises

explanation: Good catch! Resting weight in the armpits can smash nerves and blood vessels. Patients must always support their weight with their hands.

question: Which design offers the highest level of evidence by using all three core elements?

options.A: True experimental design
options.B: Quasi-experimental design
options.C: Pre-experimental design
options.D: Descriptive survey design

explanation: True experiments use manipulation, control, and randomization together, making their findings the most trustworthy for clinical guidelines. [learn more](GNS224_U1_T7#GNS224_U1_T7_h3)

question: Why is it smart not to throw away the broth after boiling vegetables?

options.A: It slows down digestion so much that hunger never returns
options.B: It neutralizes all harmful bacteria that may have survived the cooking process
options.C: It recaptures water-soluble vitamins and minerals that leaked out during boiling
options.D: It provides all the dietary protein required for the day in one serving

explanation: Brilliant! Drinking the soup broth ensures you don't lose all those valuable vitamins that leaked out into the water.

question: When wrapping a residual limb with an elastic bandage, where should the pressure be tightest?

options.A: At the bottom end of the stump
options.B: Equally tight all the way up
options.C: Near the top of the joint
options.D: Across the middle portion

explanation: Wrapping tighter at the bottom (distal end) pushes fluid upward and helps shape the limb into a neat cone, which makes fitting a prosthesis much easier later.

question: What primary change in the maternal circulatory system causes physiological hemodilution during pregnancy?

options.A: Red blood cell production completely stops during the third trimester
options.B: Blood vessels shrink in diameter to speed up flow
options.C: Total body water decreases while iron stores multiply
options.D: Plasma volume increases much more than red blood cell mass

explanation: The fluid portion of blood expands significantly faster than actual red blood cells are manufactured, creating a dilutional effect. [learn more](GNS226_U4_T009#GNS226_U4_T009_h2)

question: What is the main goal of community nursing advocacy for smoke-free indoor public spaces?

options.A: To protect non-smokers and children from the dangers of secondhand smoke
options.B: To help current smokers reduce their daily cigarette count
options.C: To reduce the government spending on imported medical supplies
options.D: To eliminate all tobacco farming in rural agricultural areas

explanation: Smoke-free rules ensure that people who don't smoke aren't forced to breathe in harmful tobacco smoke. Amazing job completing this session!

question: Why must everyone step back and not touch the patient while the AED is analyzing?

options.A: Movement can interfere with accurate rhythm analysis by the device
options.B: To prevent the rescuer from getting accidentally shocked
options.C: It gives the resuscitation team more physical room to work
options.D: Touching the patient increases the electrical output of the machine

explanation: Any motion or shaking can trick the smart computer inside the AED into misreading the heart rhythm. Staying clear keeps the reading accurate!

question: Which lab test is a key indicator that cells are lacking oxygen and relying on backup energy pathways?

options.A: Blood lactate level
options.B: Serum sodium level
options.C: Total serum protein
options.D: Platelet count

explanation: Lactate builds up like exhaust smoke when cells are starved of oxygen and forced into anaerobic metabolism. Checking blood lactate is a quick way to see how severe the tissue oxygen shortage is.

question: What is an important nursing check before preparing an infant for a scheduled circumcision?

options.A: Starting an intravenous line in the foot
options.B: Checking when the baby last fed
options.C: Shaving the entire pubic and scrotal hair
options.D: Administering a full dose of oral antibiotics

explanation: Checking the last feeding time helps prevent the baby from vomiting and potentially choking (aspirating) while being handled during the procedure.

question: A remote Nigerian village has no government clinic and relies heavily on a local mission hospital for maternity care. What type of organization is running this hospital?

options.A: Commercial pharmaceutical firm
options.B: Faith-Based Organization
options.C: Advocacy NGO
options.D: Global regulatory body

explanation: Mission hospitals run by religious groups are faith-based organizations, and they play a massive role in bringing healthcare to rural communities.

question: In simple terms, what does epidemiology study?

options.A: The distribution and determinants of diseases in populations
options.B: The microscopic structure of human body tissues
options.C: The chemical composition of pharmaceutical drugs
options.D: The financial management of healthcare institutions

explanation: You got it! Epidemiology is basically disease detective work—it figures out who is getting sick, why it's happening, and how sickness spreads.

question: Why is being kind and compassionate so important when caring for a PAC patient?

options.A: It prevents the physical pain caused by uterine contractions
options.B: It shortens the standard hospital stay to less than two hours
options.C: It completely eliminates the need for any antibiotic therapy
options.D: It reduces anxiety and encourages honest disclosure of medical history

explanation: When patients feel safe and free from judgment, they are much more likely to share true details that help us care for them better.

question: Which of these details is typically recorded in the stock inventory part of the safety form?

options.A: The personal home address of every patient
options.B: Opening balance and quantities used
options.C: Detailed medical diagnoses of injection recipients
options.D: Daily weather conditions at the facility

explanation: Correct! The stock section is strictly about numbers: what we started with, what we used, and what is left.

question: In the SBAR communication tool, what does the letter 'B' stand for?

options.A: Bedside
options.B: Background
options.C: Behavior
options.D: Balance

explanation: Awesome! 'B' is for Background, which gives the history and context leading up to the current situation.

question: Which of these is NOT a typical complication of an untreated liver hydatid cyst?

options.A: Rupture into the peritoneal cavity
options.B: Biliary tract obstruction
options.C: Permanent vision loss
options.D: Secondary bacterial infection

explanation: Liver cysts cause tummy, bile duct, and belly issues—they don't mess with your eyesight!

question: Why does the body increase blood volume so massively during pregnancy?

options.A: To store extra calcium needed for the baby's developing bones
options.B: To increase the physical strength of the maternal heart muscle
options.C: To provide extra fluid protection against blood loss during delivery
options.D: To completely prevent the mother from ever catching infections

explanation: Nature is amazing! The extra blood acts as a safety cushion for the blood loss that naturally happens when giving birth. Brilliant design, right?

question: Up to how many weeks of pregnancy can a standard medical abortion safely be done?

options.A: Up to 20 to 22 weeks
options.B: Anytime during the first trimester only
options.C: Up to 10 to 11 weeks
options.D: Strictly within the first 4 weeks

explanation: Spot on! Medical abortion is most effective and safest when used within the first 10 to 11 weeks of pregnancy.

question: What is the primary reason nurses must master drug dosage calculations?

options.A: To reduce the workload of the hospital pharmacy
options.B: To speed up the hospital discharge process
options.C: To prevent medication errors and keep patients safe
options.D: To replace the need for physician order sheets

explanation: Accurate calculations ensure the patient receives the exact therapeutic amount, avoiding underdosing or dangerous toxicity. [learn more](GNS125_U2_T6#GNS125_U2_T6_h1)

question: How is community health nursing different from working inside a hospital ward?

options.A: It avoids interaction with families and local groups
options.B: It prioritizes population wellness over individual acute care
options.C: It operates strictly inside enclosed clinic wards
options.D: It relies exclusively on advanced surgical interventions

explanation: Great thinking! Hospital nursing is all about getting the patient stable right by the bedside, whereas community nursing focuses on keeping the whole population well and preventing sickness.

question: What does the letter 'M' stand for in the TNM cancer staging system?

options.A: Muscle involvement
options.B: Microscopic grading
options.C: Distant metastasis
options.D: Malignant potential

explanation: Spot on! In the TNM system, M tells us if the cancer has traveled (metastasized) to distant organs far away from where it started.

question: What is the main difference between 'change' and 'transition' in a hospital setting?

options.A: Change only affects doctors, while transition only affects bedside nurses.
options.B: Change happens slowly over years, whereas transition happens instantly.
options.C: Change is an external event, while transition is the internal emotional process.
options.D: Change is psychological, while transition is purely structural.

explanation: Brilliant distinction! Change is the physical new policy or machine, while transition is how our minds and hearts catch up to it.

question: A nurse thinks safety rules only matter in big factories and ignores small offices in the building. Where is the mistake in this thinking?

options.A: Nursing councils have no say over non-manufacturing environments
options.B: Administrative offices are completely exempt from all laws
options.C: Workplace safety regulations extend to offices and small-scale enterprises as well
options.D: Only human resources are responsible for office building safety

explanation: Spot on! Safety laws apply everywhere people work—even in small offices, not just heavy industries.

question: If a country relies heavily on importing most of its food, what is the biggest risk to its food supply?

options.A: Local soil becoming too fertile to grow native food crops
options.B: Farmers in the home country producing too much surplus grain locally
options.C: Global shipping disruptions and sudden price spikes on international markets
options.D: Citizens losing their appetite for imported grain products over time

explanation: When you depend on other nations for food, any global shipping crisis or sudden price jump hits your country hard.

question: When should a nurse researcher use the median instead of the mean?

options.A: When the data contains extreme outliers or is heavily skewed
options.B: When every single data point needs to be included in the calculation
options.C: When working exclusively with large, perfectly symmetrical bell curves
options.D: When the data represents simple categorical groups with no numbers

explanation: The median ignores extreme highs and lows, giving you a much truer picture of the center when your data is lopsided.

question: When we talk about resource mobilization for a project, what does it include besides money?

options.A: Gathering medical supplies, outreach spaces, and local volunteers
options.B: Closing down existing health posts to save money
options.C: Reducing the number of staff required to run the clinic
options.D: Waiting for international organizations to supply all equipment

explanation: Resources aren't just cash in hand. They include everything from a good venue for outreach to willing volunteers and basic supplies.

question: What is the main job of the appendicular skeleton?

options.A: Maintaining the central structural axis for upright balance
options.B: Protecting the delicate structures of the central nervous system
options.C: Facilitating body movement and interacting with the environment
options.D: Housing the bone marrow that produces white blood cells

explanation: The appendicular skeleton includes your arms, legs, and shoulders—built for moving around and grabbing things!

question: What is the correct sequence when putting on personal protective equipment before entering an isolation room?

options.A: Eye protection, gloves, gown, mask
options.B: Gloves, gown, mask, eye protection
options.C: Gown, mask, eye protection, gloves
options.D: Mask, gloves, gown, eye protection

explanation: Putting the gown on first and gloves last ensures the glove cuffs overlap the gown sleeves, leaving no exposed skin at the wrist. [learn more](GNS123_U4_T4#GNS123_U4_T4_h6)

question: How does the body respond during a negative energy balance?

options.A: It burns stored fat and tissue to meet energy needs.
options.B: It stops all metabolic processes completely.
options.C: It increases total body mass rapidly.
options.D: It stores all incoming nutrients directly as fat.

explanation: When you burn more than you eat, the body cleverly taps into its stored fat and tissues for backup power, leading to weight loss.

question: Which clinical signs are classic clues that a patient's liver is struggling to excrete bilirubin properly?

options.A: Dark urine and pale, clay-colored stools
options.B: Extreme sensitivity to bright outdoor light
options.C: Bright red spots scattered over the chest
options.D: Swelling in the lower legs and ankles

explanation: Think about the pathway: if bile can't reach the intestines, stool loses its brown colour, and the excess bilirubin spills out through the kidneys, making the urine very dark.

question: What is the main reason nurses connect family caregivers with respite care services?

options.A: To prevent caregiver burnout and exhaustion
options.B: To reduce the financial cost of home medical equipment
options.C: To permanently transfer legal responsibility for the patient
options.D: To train family members to become licensed nurses

explanation: Looking after a stroke survivor is tough work. Respite care gives families a well-deserved break to rest and recharge!

question: A ward manager notices more patient falls happening. What should they do right after gathering this data?

options.A: Write a brand new job description for the ward clerk
options.B: Ignore the data until the end of the fiscal year audit
options.C: Compare the fall rates against the established hospital safety benchmark
options.D: Immediately fire the nurses working the night shift without investigation

explanation: Once you collect the data, the logical next step is to compare it to your hospital's safety standard to see how big the gap is.

question: What creates that scratchy 'pericardial friction rub' sound heard through a stethoscope?

options.A: Blood leaking backward through a faulty valve
options.B: Blood rushing too fast through narrowed coronary arteries
options.C: Rough, inflamed heart sac layers rubbing against each other
options.D: Air trapped inside the chest cavity

explanation: Think of it like sandpaper: when the pericardial layers get rough from inflammation, they scratch against each other with every heartbeat, creating that distinct sound. [learn more](GNS213_U1_T7#GNS213_U1_T7_h2)

question: A new trauma patient is struggling to breathe and has no breath sounds on the right side. Using ABCDE, what is your next step after checking the airway?

options.A: Breathing
options.B: Disability
options.C: Circulation
options.D: Exposure

explanation: We always follow the strict ABCDE order. Once the airway (A) is clear, breathing (B) is your immediate next focus!

question: What exactly is a paralytic ileus?

options.A: Rapid twisting of the sigmoid colon
options.B: Severe infection of the appendix lining
options.C: Temporary stoppage of intestinal peristalsis after surgery
options.D: A permanent blockage caused by a large tumor

explanation: Sometimes the bowel goes to sleep after abdominal surgery and temporarily stops moving. It's a common post-op watch-out for nurses!

question: How do multidisciplinary ward rounds help improve rational drug use?

options.A: They eliminate the need for keeping written patient medical records
options.B: They reduce the number of patients admitted to the emergency department
options.C: Doctors, nurses, and pharmacists review drug necessity together to catch errors early
options.D: They allow nurses to bypass doctors and prescribe medications independently

explanation: Collaboration across disciplines brings different perspectives together, ensuring safer and more rational medication orders. [learn more](GNS223_U3_T9#GNS223_U3_T9_h7)

question: How does fragmented healthcare (visiting different clinics without coordination) lead to polypharmacy?

options.A: Government policies limit the number of drugs a clinic can buy at once.
options.B: Different specialists prescribe drugs without knowing what other doctors ordered.
options.C: Patients intentionally hide their pill bottles from nurses during ward rounds.
options.D: Pharmacists refuse to dispense medicines prescribed by general practitioners.

explanation: When doctors don't talk to each other, a patient might end up getting duplicate or conflicting drugs from different specialists. Communication is key!

question: Why is feeling things through your skin so important for everyday survival?

options.A: It provides the primary energy source for epidermal cells.
options.B: It alerts the body to immediate physical dangers in the environment.
options.C: It prevents the accumulation of lactic acid in muscle tissue.
options.D: It controls the hormonal output of the pituitary gland.

explanation: Spot on! Being able to feel pain or extreme heat and cold lets your body react in a flash to avoid serious injury.

question: What is an effective community nursing strategy to help stop FGM?

options.A: Inspecting every household's private rooms every single week
options.B: Punishing mothers publicly for crimes committed by elders
options.C: Banning all community meetings and traditional gatherings in villages
options.D: Promoting alternative rites of passage that celebrate maturity without cutting

explanation: Spot on! Offering safe, positive ways to celebrate cultural milestones helps communities keep their traditions alive while dropping the dangerous cutting.

question: Which chemical is standard for high-level disinfection of flexible endoscopes that cannot handle high heat?

options.A: Dilute isopropyl alcohol
options.B: Glutaraldehyde and OPA
options.C: Quaternary ammonium compounds
options.D: Soap and warm water

explanation: Endoscopes would melt in an autoclave! Heat-sensitive scopes are safely disinfected using specialized chemicals like glutaraldehyde or OPA.

question: Why must the delivery room be kept warm and free from cold drafts?

options.A: Cold drafts increase the risk of maternal postpartum bleeding
options.B: Newborn babies quickly lose body heat and cannot shiver
options.C: Cold air causes the mother's uterine contractions to stop
options.D: Warm temperatures help keep delivery instruments sterile longer

explanation: Newborns can't shiver to warm up yet! Keeping the room cozy protects them from rapid heat loss and cold stress right after birth.

question: Why should nursing researchers care about national and global health goals?

options.A: It helps secure research funding and ensures the study addresses urgent needs
options.B: It removes all ethical considerations from the research process
options.C: It eliminates the requirement to collect informed consent from patients
options.D: It guarantees that no other nurse will ever read the published paper

explanation: When your research tackles pressing real-world problems, it's easier to get support and make a true difference in society.

question: What does the term 'brain drain' mean for Nigerian healthcare?

options.A: The gradual loss of memory in elderly psychiatric patients
options.B: A neurological disease caused by severe vitamin deficiencies in adults
options.C: The closure of mental health training schools due to lack of students
options.D: The mass emigration of skilled health workers leaving facilities understaffed

explanation: Correct! Brain drain refers to trained professionals leaving the country for better opportunities abroad, which leaves our remaining hospitals and clinics understaffed.

question: A patient is officially diagnosed with AIDS when their CD4 count drops below which threshold?

options.A: 800 cells/mm3
options.B: 200 cells/mm3
options.C: 500 cells/mm3
options.D: 1000 cells/mm3

explanation: A CD4 count falling below 200 cells/mm3 marks the transition from chronic HIV infection to a diagnosis of AIDS. [learn more](GNS214_U1_T4#GNS214_U1_T4_h3)

question: What unit of measurement is typically used when programming an electronic infusion pump?

options.A: Drops per minute (gtt/min)
options.B: Milligrams per minute (mg/min)
options.C: Milliliters per hour (mL/hr)
options.D: Liters per 24 hours (L/day)

explanation: Electronic infusion pumps are calibrated to deliver exact volumetric amounts calculated in milliliters per hour. [learn more](GNS122_U1_T16#GNS122_U1_T16_h6)

question: Why is it a drawback to keep a successful quality project locked inside just one nursing unit?

options.A: It prevents other patients and staff from benefiting from proven safer practices
options.B: It causes the original unit to lose funding for their nursing supplies
options.C: It automatically violates hospital licensing and accreditation standards
options.D: It forces the hospital to hire extra consultants from outside the country

explanation: Sharing is caring in nursing! When we keep great improvements hidden in one ward, other patients miss out on safer care.

question: What do we call a neuron that has one main axon and many dendrites branching out?

options.A: Unipolar neuron
options.B: Anaxonic neuron
options.C: Multipolar neuron
options.D: Bipolar neuron

explanation: Since it has multiple extensions (one axon plus many dendrites), it's called a multipolar neuron. These are the most common type in our nervous system!

question: Why do nurses avoid using chemical names of drugs during routine clinical practice?

options.A: Chemical names change every time a new company manufactures the drug
options.B: Chemical names are strictly reserved for pharmacy dispensing staff only
options.C: Chemical names are too complex and difficult to use safely in daily care
options.D: Chemical names only describe the inactive filler ingredients in the tablet

explanation: Chemical names are full of complex molecular descriptions. Imagine trying to read one out quickly during an emergency ward round—way too tricky! That's why we stick to generic and brand names.

question: Since there is no cure for established paralytic polio, what is the main goal of treatment?

options.A: Immediate surgical repair of damaged motor neurons
options.B: Supportive care and complication prevention
options.C: Direct antiviral elimination of the virus from nerves
options.D: Aggressive immune suppression therapy

explanation: Exactly right! We focus heavily on keeping the patient comfortable, managing pain, and preventing long-term body stiffness.

question: Which screening tool is commonly used to check for delirium in ventilated ICU patients?

options.A: Glasgow Coma Scale
options.B: Apgar Score
options.C: CAM-ICU
options.D: Braden Scale

explanation: The CAM-ICU (Confusion Assessment Method for the ICU) is specifically built to help us catch delirium even when patients can't talk.

question: Why is proper sample collection and transport so important in the lab?

options.A: It eliminates the need for any laboratory staining procedures
options.B: It prevents sample contamination and keeps the pathogen alive for testing
options.C: It cures the patient's infection before the lab results arrive
options.D: It ensures the laboratory bills the correct insurance company

explanation: You got it! If a sample gets contaminated or mishandled on its way to the lab, we might test the wrong thing and give the patient the wrong care.

question: How does the medication simethicone help relieve gas?

options.A: It paralyzes the bowel muscles to stop cramping completely.
options.B: It neutralizes all stomach acid to prevent digestion.
options.C: It combines small gas bubbles into larger ones that are easier to expel.
options.D: It permanently stops all bacteria from living in the large intestine.

explanation: Simethicone is a neat little helper that rounds up tiny trapped gas bubbles into bigger ones so the body can pass them easily.

question: A mother looks anxious and confused about why her baby needs multiple injections. As a nurse, what is your best approach?

options.A: Scold her for not knowing the routine immunization schedule already
options.B: Administer the injections quickly without speaking to avoid argument
options.C: Tell her to come back another day when she is better prepared
options.D: Patiently explain the purpose of each vaccine and welcome her questions

explanation: Wonderful nursing care! Warm communication and health education build trust, making parents feel supported and ready to complete vaccination.

question: What are personal objectives in the workplace?

options.A: Strict penalties for arriving late to morning handover
options.B: Mandatory government targets for patient bed occupancy
options.C: Secret rules created by the hospital board of directors
options.D: Individual goals that workers bring with them to their jobs

explanation: Personal objectives are all about what YOU want for yourself, like gaining new clinical skills, getting a promotion, or personal growth.

question: During a disease outbreak, which of these is a core duty for a community health nurse?

options.A: Writing national health policies and approving federal budgets
options.B: Isolating entire towns by deploying armed security forces
options.C: Conducting contact tracing and educating community members on prevention
options.D: Manufacturing vaccines inside local primary health care clinics

explanation: You got it! Nurses are right on the frontline—tracking down contacts, teaching families how to stay safe, and helping at the grassroots level.

question: Why do we classify mental health symptoms into categories?

options.A: To provide a permanent cure for mental illness
options.B: To replace the need for patient interviews
options.C: To replace laboratory testing in all hospitals
options.D: To organize complex symptoms into structured categories

explanation: Grouping similar symptoms together helps you make sense of a client's presentation so you can manage their care easily. You've got this!

question: A patient asks why they got an autoimmune disease while their sibling living in the same house did not. What best explains this?

options.A: Viral infections only affect the oldest sibling in a family
options.B: Differences in genetic susceptibility and individual environmental triggers
options.C: Autoimmune diseases are entirely contagious between household members
options.D: The sibling must have a stronger immune system due to diet

explanation: Even in the same house, no two people have the exact same genes or identical life exposures, which changes everyone's unique disease risk.

question: Why is simple washing not considered true sterilization?

options.A: Soap chemically alters surgical steel and ruins the instruments
options.B: Washing only removes dirt and some microbes without killing spores
options.C: Cleaning actually introduces more bacteria to the equipment
options.D: Washing uses cold water which activates bacterial growth

explanation: Washing is a great first step to get the dirt off, but it leaves tough little spores behind. Sterilization finishes the job!

question: What happens during 'data cleaning' after data collection?

options.A: Checking for entry mistakes, missing fields, and unusual outlier values
options.B: Translating all interview recordings into a different spoken language
options.C: Deleting any participant answers that do not support the hypothesis
options.D: Washing physical paper questionnaires with soap to remove hospital dust

explanation: Data cleaning means scanning your data for typos, blank spots, or weird errors before you start analyzing.

question: Which brain wave pattern takes over during deep, restful slow-wave sleep?

options.A: Alpha waves
options.B: Delta waves
options.C: Beta waves
options.D: Gamma waves

explanation: Delta waves are slow and tall, showing up during deep sleep when your body gets its best physical rest.

question: How does a mother's education level usually affect her children's health?

options.A: Educated mothers spend less time taking care of their children at home
options.B: Educated mothers are more likely to understand immunization schedules and hygiene
options.C: Uneducated mothers have better access to modern hospital equipment
options.D: Mothers with schooling rarely experience childhood illnesses in their families

explanation: That's right! Mums who have been to school find it easier to follow health guidelines, leading to better handwashing, timely vaccinations, and healthier kids.

question: Why are grab bars installed in bathrooms for individuals with physical disabilities?

options.A: To block water from splashing onto the bathroom floor tiles
options.B: To hold towels and washcloths within easy reach of the bathing area
options.C: To serve as hanging storage for lightweight assistive devices
options.D: To provide stable support during transfers on and off the toilet or in the shower

explanation: Wet bathroom surfaces combined with transfers make grab bars essential safety features for preventing falls. [learn more](GNS225_U5_T9#GNS225_U5_T9_h5)

question: Which of these is a major headache for tracking nursing costs in many Nigerian hospitals?

options.A: Excessive use of automated digital billing
options.B: Reliance on manual record-keeping systems
options.C: Universal health insurance coverage for all citizens
options.D: Complete elimination of out-of-pocket purchases

explanation: When everything is on paper, it becomes very difficult to quickly track exact nursing hours and supplies used.

question: A patient leaks a little urine whenever she coughs or sneezes. Which pelvic floor function has failed here?

options.A: Continence support during increased pressure
options.B: Complete relaxation during bladder emptying
options.C: Core stabilization for the spinal column
options.D: Sexual sensation enhancement

explanation: You got it! This is called stress incontinence—when the pelvic floor isn't strong or fast enough to close the urethra against sudden pressure like a sneeze.

question: Why is rapid treatment so critical for a patient with cholera?

options.A: It prevents the spread of airborne droplets
options.B: Antibiotics stop chronic liver failure instantly
options.C: Severe fluid loss can cause death within hours
options.D: Delayed care causes permanent paralysis

explanation: The rapid loss of body water and salts can quickly lead to shock if we don't replace it right away. Quick action saves lives!

question: What is a major risk for family members who care for a loved one long-term without a break?

options.A: Sudden medical immunity
options.B: Instant financial wealth
options.C: Caregiver burnout
options.D: Complete loss of empathy

explanation: Looking after someone takes a massive physical and emotional toll. Always remember to check on the caregivers too—they need support to stay strong!

question: Why should a nurse emphasize that tubal ligation is permanent even though microsurgical reversals exist?

options.A: Reversal operations always cause permanent damage to the ovaries and uterus.
options.B: The human fallopian tubes instantly dissolve once they are surgically cut.
options.C: Reversal surgery is expensive, complex, and has uncertain success rates.
options.D: Hospitals legally forbid patients from ever attempting to reverse the procedure.

explanation: Reversing a tubal ligation requires delicate microsurgery that is not always successful, making it unwise for patients to rely on it as a backup plan. [learn more](GNS226_U6_T019#GNS226_U6_T019_h7)

question: Which of the following is NOT true about integrating different types of healthcare plans?

options.A: Alignment between plans helps prevent wasted resources
options.B: Nurse managers must communicate both upward and downward
options.C: Strategic, tactical, and operational plans must work together
options.D: Operational plans can completely contradict strategic goals without consequence

explanation: Operational plans must support strategic goals, not contradict them, for the organization to succeed. [learn more](GST321_U1_T6#GST321_U1_T6_h6)

question: Which of these is a key feature of teacher-centred teaching methods?

options.A: The classroom has no formal structure or predefined schedule
options.B: The teacher observes quietly while students teach each other
options.C: The students spend all class time performing independent research
options.D: The educator acts as the primary information giver while learners listen

explanation: In a teacher-centred setup (like a classic lecture), the instructor does most of the talking and passes information directly to the listening students.

question: Why is splitting funds across federal, state, and local governments a big problem in Nigeria's health system?

options.A: It prevents international donors from sending any financial aid
options.B: It makes tracking spending and resource distribution difficult
options.C: It forces all private hospitals to close down immediately
options.D: It automatically increases out-of-pocket payments by fifty percent

explanation: When money comes from many uncoordinated sources, it becomes tough to manage efficiently or ensure it actually reaches grassroots clinics. Spotting these system gaps is key for a brilliant nurse!

question: A nurse cares for an immobile surgery patient who is showing poor wound healing and muscle wasting. What is the most likely cause?

options.A: Inadequate nutritional intake failing to meet elevated metabolic demands
options.B: Too much physical exercise during the early post-operative phase
options.C: Excessive thyroid hormone production caused by routine bed rest
options.D: An accidental drop in the patient's core body temperature overnight

explanation: Surgery spikes the body's need for fuel. If the patient isn't getting enough nutrition, the body starts breaking down its own muscle and tissue to survive, stalling recovery.

question: Under Nigerian law, what is the main legal ground that allows for a safe and lawful termination of pregnancy?

options.A: When the pregnancy results from consensual sex
options.B: Upon the request of both parents
options.C: To save the life of the pregnant woman
options.D: In cases of severe economic hardship

explanation: You've got this! Nigerian law is very strict, allowing pregnancy termination only when it is necessary to preserve the mother's life.

question: A patient says, 'My life is completely useless.' The nurse replies, 'You feel that your life has no meaning right now?' What communication skill is this?

options.A: Defending an institutional rule
options.B: Giving premature advice
options.C: Changing the conversation subject
options.D: Reflecting the patient's statement

explanation: Brilliant! Reflecting means repeating or paraphrasing the patient's feelings back to them. It shows you are actively listening and encourages them to open up more.

question: A nurse is planning care for a newly admitted patient with severe depression and a history of job loss. What should the nursing care plan include?

options.A: Strict bed rest with zero communication until the patient asks for help
options.B: Telling the patient to forget about their job loss and think positively
options.C: Both biological treatments like medication and social support for coping with stress
options.D: Discharging the patient immediately before addressing any emotional issues

explanation: Because mental disorders have multiple causes, effective nursing care combines medical, psychological, and social interventions. [learn more](GNS314_U2_T4#GNS314_U2_T4_h8)

question: Why might relying only on the hospital's liability insurance leave you unprotected as a nurse?

options.A: Institutional coverage automatically pays out cash settlements directly to the nurse
options.B: Hospital attorneys represent the institution and may have interests conflicting with the nurse's
options.C: Employer policies never cover mistakes made during night shifts
options.D: Facility insurance policies expire the moment a nurse takes a short break

explanation: Remember, the hospital's legal team works for the hospital, not you! Their main job is protecting the facility, so having your own backup is smart nursing practice.

question: What tough, fibrous layer of connective tissue tightly wraps around the corpora cavernosa to give it support?

options.A: Endothelial lining
options.B: Perineal membrane
options.C: Tunica albuginea
options.D: Trabecular fascia

explanation: You got this! The tunica albuginea is a strong, fibrous covering that acts like a supportive sleeve around the corpora cavernosa during an erection.

question: Why is it so important to build quick rapport with a patient right at the start of an interview?

options.A: It prevents the patient from asking any difficult questions
options.B: It shortens the total time needed for the physical exam
options.C: It guarantees the patient will follow all medication orders
options.D: It lowers patient anxiety and encourages honest sharing

explanation: Exactly! When patients feel safe and respected by you, they relax and open up about what is truly bothering them.

question: When is the best time for a first follow-up visit after putting in an IUD (Intrauterine Device)?

options.A: After six months
options.B: After exactly five years
options.C: After twenty-four hours
options.D: After four to six weeks

explanation: Seeing the client at 4 to 6 weeks lets you check the IUD strings and make sure the device hasn't slipped out.

question: What is the main job of Phase I metabolic reactions?

options.A: To build brand new proteins from scratch inside the bloodstream
options.B: To store extra vitamins inside the liver cells for later use
options.C: To introduce or uncover a polar functional group on the drug molecule
options.D: To attach a large bulky sugar molecule to trap the drug in fat

explanation: Phase I is all about tweaking the drug slightly—adding or exposing a little chemical handle (a polar group) so the body can grab onto it for the next steps.
